plan.name: Attribute supplied component conformance
plan.summary: Add an independent supplied conformance API and JSON records for exact production targets, selected canonical checks and invocations, retaining actual outcomes, runner pins, declaration and execution-input snapshots, model identity, ratified bounds, ordered observations and separate attempt coverage. Qualify successful transition, exhaustive-state and every-step evidence without changing supplied mode or outcome: sampled runs never establish exhaustive states, absent attempts establish no every-step claim, and unsuccessful attempts block exhaustive states while preserving successful checked transitions. Make all three attribution APIs detached atomic replacements that revalidate every retained kind, including incomplete attempts and outside-scope driver, model, include, bounds-source and invocation changes, while preserving old proof callers, complete production proof rows, gate outcomes, legacy checks and ratified data. Deep-copy and canonically fingerprint every new semantic value and set, including decoded reports, preserving meaningful sequences, relocation stability and legacy outputs; run no tools, discover no omitted inputs and keep explicit component verification unavailable. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the API, JSON, provenance matching, coverage distinctions, replacement rules, fingerprint inputs and Markdown's limited proof view, cite supporting decisions including D-0169 on changed SPEC bullets, and state that the merger must record the new conformance attribution policy because the plumbing build cannot write decisions/; preserve pinned statements and ratified locks.

tests.name: TestSuppliedConformanceSeparatesStatesTransitionsAndAttempts
tests.says: Sampled and bounded-exhaustive supplied records distinguish checked transitions, exhaustive state coverage and every-step attempts across absent, failed, timed-out, skipped, empty and successful attempts and positive matching, mismatched and zero state counts, retaining the actual mode and outcomes.

tests.name: TestSuppliedConformanceRequiresActualSuccessfulCompleteEvidence
tests.says: Failed, timed-out, skipped, empty, missing and incomplete actual outcomes cannot become successful evidence from positive counts, declarations or legacy package success; missing runner, exercised checks, declaration snapshots, execution files, model or bounds provenance remain visible as unchecked.

tests.name: TestSuppliedConformanceUsesExactSelectedChecksAndInvocations
tests.says: Canonical production targets, multiple selected checks and repeated invocation identities remain distinct, outside-scope drivers add provenance only, complete production proof rows stay unchecked without proof, and JSON preserves component-only assurance.

tests.name: TestSuppliedConformanceRejectsInvalidAttributionAtomically
tests.says: Unknown, duplicate, bare-name, unselected, stale and late-batch references, mismatched model/bounds or invocation metadata and invalid inventories reject without changing serialized report bytes or stored and recomputed fingerprints.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceIndependentReplacementAndClear
tests.says: All six proof, assumption and conformance attribution orders under both gate outcomes replace and clear only their own evidence kind, preserve legacy checks and ratified data, retain complete proof coverage and produce the same final JSON and fingerprint.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceRetainsLegacyProofCompatibility
tests.says: Proof callers without execution metadata still accept extra known verified declarations, checked contracts and matching snapshots before or after conformance, and remain valid through conformance clearing without transferring proof.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceRevalidatedOnProofAndAssumptionUpdates
tests.says: Proof and assumption replacement or clearing atomically reject complete or incomplete retained conformance invalidated by outside-scope drivers, targets, contracts, selections, invocation metadata, non-Go data, dependencies, model/include/lock snapshots or report bounds.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceUpdatesRevalidateRetainedProofsAndAssumptions
tests.says: Conformance replacement or clearing rejects retained stale proof, including incomplete attempts, or assumed records even when the replacement inventory and incoming conformance are independently valid.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceFingerprintBindsEverySuppliedField
tests.says: Fingerprints of decoded reports bind every new conformance and attempt field, presence, outcome, count, mode, observation, declaration and file hash, invocation value, runner pin and model/bounds source without mutating the report.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceCanonicalSetsSequencesAndRelocation
tests.says: Storage and decoded-report fingerprints canonicalize inventory and record completion order and reference sets, remain stable across checkout relocation, preserve ordered arguments, observations and diagnostics, and retain volatile exclusions.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceOwnsActualTypedArgumentsAndInventory
tests.says: Mutating actual typed caller results or inventories, including nested invocation maps, file/model/bounds snapshots, observations, attempts, runner pins and diagnostics, cannot change stored report bytes or fingerprints.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceAttributionNeverExecutesAndModelOnlyRejectsIt
tests.says: Sentinel commands confirm attribution and clearing execute nothing, Check and Run still reject explicit components with ErrComponents before tools start, model-only checking remains available, and model-only reports reject conformance attribution atomically.

tests.name: TestComponentConformanceMarkdownRemainsAProofView
tests.says: Explicit Markdown retains proof-only coverage and its supplied-data/assumption footer while conformance and attempt details remain in JSON; successful legacy receipts, JSON and fingerprints remain unchanged.

usage.summary: Wrote [plan.json](plan.json) and 13 acceptance tests covering conformance attribution, coverage distinctions, atomic updates, provenance, and compatibility. The first check passed: all acceptance tests fail on the base code as required, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
